Library Lending

A small public library lends books to its members. Members borrow a copy, keep it for a fixed loan period, and pay a late fee when they return it after the due date. This example exists to exercise every concept of the meta-model in one place, across every stage of the life cycle; it is not a real library's system.

Version 0.1.0; meta-model 0.1; stages requirements, design, implementation, tests, deployment, commissioning, operation; owners example-maintainers.

Approval: not approved: there is no records/approvals/0.1.0.yaml beside the specification

0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 open questions; each is listed under Problems and marked at the entry it concerns.

Requirements

Stakeholders /stakeholders

librarian /stakeholders/librarian

description
Staff at the desk who register members, lend copies and take returns.
concerns

Every desk task fits in one screen and takes under a minute., A fee is never wrong by a cent.

member /stakeholders/member

description
A card holder who borrows books.
concerns

Only their own loans and fees are shown to them., They are told when a loan is overdue.

library-board /stakeholders/library-board

description
The board that sets the lending policy and answers to the regulator.
concerns

The policy sheet and the system agree., Member data is kept as the rules allow and no longer.

Needs /needs

NEED-1 /needs/NEED-1

Note: From Interview with the desk staff about lending and returns: The card index is searched by hand when a member asks what they have out, and it is often out of date.

statement
We need to know who has which copy and when it is due, without a card index.
stakeholders

librarian

status
accepted

status
accepted

Glossary /glossary

Name definition
copy /glossary/copy One physical book. The example counts copies per title and does not identify them.
tier /glossary/tier A membership level that sets the loan limit and the loan period.
loan period /glossary/loan period The number of days a copy may be kept; 21 for the standard tier, 28 for the extended tier.
late fee /glossary/late fee The amount charged when a copy comes back after its due date.

Assumptions /assumptions

ASSUME-1 /assumptions/ASSUME-1

statement
One library, one branch, one currency.

ASSUME-2 /assumptions/ASSUME-2

Note: From Lending policy of the library, 2026, clause 4: The board sets the daily rate once a year.

statement
The daily rate changes rarely and is a library setting, not a per-book value.

Constraints /constraints

CON-1 /constraints/CON-1

Note: From The data-protection rules the library is bound by, 2024: Personal data is kept no longer than its purpose needs.

statement
Member data is kept only while the membership is open and for one year after, then deleted.
kind
legal

CON-2 /constraints/CON-2

Insight: A loan due on the 21st is overdue from the start of the 22nd, library time, whatever the server's clock.

statement
Dates are the library's local calendar dates; timestamps are UTC.
kind
technical

Dependencies /dependencies

feeLedger /dependencies/feeLedger

Insight: The desk waits for the answer, so a call that takes longer than a few seconds is given up and the return is refused rather than left half done.

description
The finance system's ledger, where a late fee or a replacement charge is posted the moment it is charged.
timeout
PT5S

Jobs /jobs

markOverdue /jobs/markOverdue

Insight: Overnight, when no one is at the desk, so a loan is overdue from the first morning after its due date.

description

Every night, finds the open loans past their due date, marks each overdue, and publishes LoanOverdue for it, so the member is told.

trigger
schedule
0 2 * * *

scheduler

retries

3

Errors /errors

Name status title condition
email-taken /errors/email-taken 409 Email address already registered A member with the same email address exists.
member-not-found /errors/member-not-found 404 No such member No member has the id in the path.
lending-refused /errors/lending-refused 409 The copy cannot be lent The member is inactive, holds the most open loans their tier allows or has outstanding fees, or the book has no copy available.
loan-closed /errors/loan-closed 409 The loan is already closed The loan was returned or reported lost before.
fee-ledger-unavailable /errors/fee-ledger-unavailable 503 The fee ledger is unavailable The fee ledger failed or did not answer in time, and the loan stays as it was.
sign-in-refused /errors/sign-in-refused 401 Sign-in refused No one has the email address, or the password does not match it.
second-factor-refused /errors/second-factor-refused 401 Second factor refused The code is not the one the authenticator app shows now, or the sign-in challenge is closed after five wrong codes or five minutes.
reset-code-refused /errors/reset-code-refused 409 Reset code refused No one was sent the reset code, or it was used or has expired.

LIB-8

Algorithms and decisions

Algorithms /algorithms

lateFee /algorithms/lateFee

description

Fee charged when a copy comes back after its due date. A flat daily rate, capped so that a long-overdue book never costs more than replacing it.

inputs
Name type format minimum description precision scale
daysLate /algorithms/lateFee/inputs/daysLate integer int32 0 Whole days after dueOn; 0 when returned on time.
dailyRate /algorithms/lateFee/inputs/dailyRate string decimal Library setting, currently 0.50. 10 2
replacementCost /algorithms/lateFee/inputs/replacementCost string decimal The book's replacementCost. 10 2
output
type
string
format
decimal
precision
10
scale
2
formula
min(decimal(daysLate, 0) * dailyRate, replacementCost)
examples
  1. name
    returned on time
    inputs
    daysLate
    0
    dailyRate
    0.50
    replacementCost
    25.00
    expected
    0.00
  2. name
    one week late
    inputs
    daysLate
    7
    dailyRate
    0.50
    replacementCost
    25.00
    expected
    3.50
    note
    7 × 0.50 = 3.50, below the cap.
  3. name
    capped at replacement cost
    inputs
    daysLate
    90
    dailyRate
    0.50
    replacementCost
    25.00
    expected
    25.00
    note
    90 × 0.50 = 45.00 exceeds the 25.00 replacement cost, so the cap applies.
  4. name
    cheap book, cap reached early
    inputs
    daysLate
    10
    dailyRate
    0.50
    replacementCost
    4.00
    expected
    4.00
pseudocode

function lateFee(daysLate, dailyRate, replacementCost): if daysLate <= 0: return 0.00 fee = daysLate * dailyRate # decimal arithmetic, 2 places if fee > replacementCost: fee = replacementCost return fee

satisfies

LIB-5

Decisions /decisions

Name title status date context decision consequences satisfies
ADR-001 /decisions/ADR-001 Late fees are a flat daily rate capped at the replacement cost accepted 2026-10-07 Tiered rates (cheaper for the first week, dearer after) were considered. They are harder to explain at the desk and the difference in revenue is small for a library of this size. One daily rate for every book, capped at that book's replacement cost. The rate is a library setting, not a per-book value. The fee can be computed from three numbers and checked by hand. A very long-overdue book costs the same as a lost one, which is what we want: at that point the member should be told to treat it as lost. LIB-5
ADR-002 /decisions/ADR-002 Money is carried as decimal strings, never floats accepted 2026-10-07 JSON has no decimal type. Fees and costs must round the way a cashier expects. Every money field is `type: string, format: decimal` with `precision` and `scale`. Generators map it to the target's decimal type and the API transports it as a string. Clients must parse the string; in return no sum ever drifts by a cent.

Deployment, commissioning and operation

Environments /environments

Name description promotesTo
development /environments/development A developer's machine, with a throwaway database. staging
staging /environments/staging A copy of production the librarians try a release on before it goes live. production
production /environments/production The live system at the desk.

Configuration /configuration

Name description secret schema satisfies
dailyRate /configuration/dailyRate The late fee per day, set by the board; read by the lateFee algorithm. false {type: string, format: decimal, precision: 10, scale: 2} LIB-5
databaseUrl /configuration/databaseUrl Where the database is; it carries the password, so it comes from the host's secret store and is never written here. true {type: string, format: uri}
notificationChannelUrl /configuration/notificationChannelUrl Where the notification service listens for loan events. false {type: string, format: uri} LIB-4

Release /release

description
A release goes to staging first, where a librarian tries the desk tasks, then to production outside opening hours.
steps
  1. name
    Build and test
    action
    Build the service from the tagged commit and run every suite.
    check
    The build and every suite pass.
  2. name
    Apply migrations on staging
    action
    Apply the new migrations to the staging database.
    check
    Every migration applied, and the schema gate against the entities passes.
  3. name
    Install on staging
    action
    Install the build on staging and run the commissioning checks there.
    check
    Every check passed.
  4. name
    Install on production
    action
    Outside opening hours, apply the migrations to production and install the build.
    check
    The smoke check passes on production before the desk opens.

Rollback /rollback

description

The previous build is kept installed beside the new one, so a rollback is a switch, and migrations are written to be reversible.

steps
  1. name
    Switch back
    action
    Point the service at the previous build and restart it.
    check
    The smoke check passes and the version shown is the previous one.
  2. name
    Reverse the migrations
    action
    Run the rollback steps of every migration the release carried, newest first.
    check
    The schema gate against the previous entities passes.

Migrations /migrations

add-membership-tier /migrations/add-membership-tier

description
Every member gets a tier; existing members are standard.
steps
  1. name
    Add the column
    action
    Add the tier column to members, allowing null.
    check
    The column exists.
  2. name
    Fill it
    action
    Set tier to standard for every member whose tier is null.
    check
    No member has a null tier; the count equals the member count.
  3. name
    Make it required
    action
    Make the tier column not null.
    check
    The schema gate against Member passes.
rollback
  1. name
    Drop the column
    action
    Drop the tier column from members.
    check
    The schema gate against the previous Member passes.
satisfies

service-answers /checks/service-answers

kind
smoke
description
The installed service starts and answers the catalogue.
environment
production
steps

    check

lend-and-return /checks/lend-and-return

kind
end-to-end
description
A whole loan goes through on the real installation, with the real notification service.
environment
staging
steps
  1. name
    Register
    action
    A librarian registers a test member through member-form.
    check
    The member appears in members-list with a card number.
  2. name
    Lend
    action
    The librarian lends a copy through loan-form.
    check
    The loan is open, due in 21 days, and the notification service received LoanCreated.
  3. name
    Return late
    action
    Move the loan's due date back eight days in the staging database and record the return.
    check
    The late fee is 4.00 and the notification service received LoanReturned.
verifies

kind
security
description
A member cannot see another member's loans.
environment
staging
steps
  1. name
    List as a member
    action

    check
    Only that member's loans are answered.
verifies

catalogue-under-load /checks/catalogue-under-load

kind
performance
description
The catalogue answers fast enough at the desk's busiest hour.
environment
staging
steps
  1. name
    Load the catalogue
    action
    Call listBooks fifty times a second for five minutes.
    check
    Nine calls in ten answer within 200 milliseconds and none fails.

migrated-members /checks/migrated-members

kind
data
description
Every member migrated from the card index is present and has a tier.
environment
production
steps
  1. name
    Count
    action
    Compare the member count with the card index count.
    check
    The counts are equal and no member has a null tier.
verifies

Signoff /signoff

criteria

Every check passed on staging and the smoke and data checks passed on production., A librarian has done each desk task once on production., The record of the run is filed under records/commissioning/.

signers
  1. role
    head-librarian
    description
    Accepts for the desk.
  2. role
    library-board
    description
    Accepts for the board.

Monitors /monitors

catalogue-latency /monitors/catalogue-latency

Insight: A slow catalogue is the first thing a librarian notices, and the commissioning check measured it only once.

description
How long listBooks takes to answer at the desk.
environment
production
objective
Nine calls in ten answer within 200 milliseconds over each opening day.
verifies
